issues.body: `parse_float` maps both `INF` and `+INF` to positive infinity, but the XSD float/double special lexical representations are `INF`, `-INF`, and `NaN`; `+INF` is not one of them. This contradicts the generated module's claim that float lexical well-formedness is enforced. The round-3 datatype harness covers integer and decimal families but includes no float/double cases, so it does not catch this real-path acceptance error.
issues.fix_hint: Remove `+INF` from the accepted special forms and add generated-loader behavioral cases for both xsd:float and xsd:double covering `INF`, `-INF`, `NaN`, ordinary exponent syntax, and rejection of `+INF` plus Rust-only/non-XSD spellings.
issues.title: Floating-point validator accepts the non-XSD `+INF` lexical form

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes both round-2 major findings: String-backed integer/decimal values now pass through datatype-specific lexical validation, narrow signed integer ranges are enforced, and the generated-loader test exercises malformed unbounded integers plus signed boundaries and out-of-range values. One new correctness gap remains in the advertised floating-point lexical validation: the implementation explicitly accepts `+INF`, which is not an XSD float/double lexical representation, while the new behavioral test does not cover either floating datatype. Because this is a new major finding relative to round 2, progress is regressing under the required scale.
